requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in fishing activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Discuss the prevention of and treatment for the following health concerns that could occur while fishing: cuts and scratches, puncture wounds, insect bites, hypothermia, dehydration, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, and sunburn. (c) Explain how to remove a barbed hook that is lodged in someone's arm. (d) Name and explain five safety practices you should always follow while fishing.

pamphlet_excerpts: Hazards, First Aid & Safety: If you orsomeone in your group shows signs of a heat reaction, get to acool, shady place (p. 15).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 2: Have the person lie down with the feet, head, and shoulders slightly raised, and remove excess clothing (p. 15).

Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 3: Cool the victim any way you can (cover the person with cool, wet towels, or sponge the person with cool water; fan the person; place the victim in a stream) (p. 15).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 4: If you do not see a rapid recovery, seek medical attention right away (p. 15).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Most sunburns are first-degree burns, but prolonged exposure to the suncan cause blistering, a second-degree burn (p. 15).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Sunburn is easy to preventby applying plenty of sunscreen and clothing with a sun protection factor (SPF) rating of at least 30 (p. 15).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Reapply if you are sweating and after you have been in water (p. 15).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): A broad-brimmed hat, long-sleeved shirt, and long pantsprovide even more protection (p. 15).
